//: Recorded time ratios that bench/check-ratios.sh gates against. A measured ratio above baseline * threshold fails the build. Refresh instructions are in docs/profiling.md.
//ratios: Keyed by platform, because a ratio is only reproducible on the machine it was recorded on. A measurement with no entry here is not judged, and the run prints its measured ratio in this file's format so it can be pasted in. A platform with no entries at all is reported as UNJUDGED with exit status 3, not as ok, unless CHECK_RATIOS_ALLOW_UNJUDGED=1 is set.
//re-recorded: win-arm64/parity/double-loop, array-walk and fixnum-loop were re-recorded on 2026-09-16 on the same machine, after float literals stopped going through the constant pool, after AREF on an array-typed local reached the unboxed element path and then the hoisted element buffer, and after a tagbody that is a simple loop stopped carrying the GO dispatch. win-arm64/parity/struct-slots was re-recorded on 2026-09-16 after structure slots declared to hold an int64 moved to raw storage. win-arm64/parity/string-walk was re-recorded on 2026-09-22 after the typed character read stopped asking twice per character which of the two string backings is live and stopped checking the bound twice. win-arm64/parity/struct-slots was re-recorded again on 2026-09-22, median of three quiet runs (1.74, 1.74, 1.73), after a structure's raw slot array started being fetched once per binding instead of on every access. win-arm64/parity/fib was re-recorded on 2026-09-22, median of the same three runs (2.44, 2.43, 2.39): it had never been re-recorded and sat at 4.00 against a measurement of 2.4, so the gate had 62 percent of slack and could not have caught a regression. Two notes from those runs. The machine is about 3 percent slower than when the 2026-09-14 set was taken (tak measured 2.34 against its recorded 2.26), so a row re-recorded now carries that and a row left alone does not. And string-walk is the noisiest kernel in the set, spreading 2.18 to 2.37 across the three, so a reading near 2.4 there is the kernel and not a regression. win-arm64/parity/array-walk was re-recorded on 2026-09-22, 0.83 to 0.89, after the array element-buffer hoist started declining vectors whose storage can be replaced under the binding: an adjustable or fill-pointered vector is no longer hoisted, and the loop body is emitted twice so the fast copy keeps its original inner loop. The inner loop is byte-identical and the cost is not in it; the function grew from 456 to 1356 bytes and the 6.8 percent is in the layout around it, measured over ten alternating pairs with the untouched kernels flat. Part of the old figure was the defect itself, which hoisted an adjustable vector as fast as a simple one while losing writes to it. win-arm64/parity/string-walk-vector was recorded on 2026-09-22 at 6.87, the first entry for that kernel, middle of three passes on a quiet box. linux-x64/parity/double-loop was re-recorded on 2026-10-01 at 1.00, the median of the five nightly and manual full CI runs from 2026-09-29 to 2026-09-30 (0.99, 0.99, 1.00, 1.00, 1.00; ci-runner-2 once, ci-runner-3 four times), after a native float local read out of a loop stopped being boxed inline: on System V x64 the inline allocation made the accumulator live across a call with no callee-saved XMM register, so it was spilled and reloaded on every iteration. The old 1.50 was that spill. Every other entry is from the run described under "recorded".

recorded.win-arm64: 2026-09-14, Snapdragon X Plus X1P42100 (Qualcomm Oryon), 8 cores, Windows 11 ARM64, .NET SDK 10.0.302, median of 3 make bench-parity runs (which agreed to within 5%)
recorded.linux-x64: Median of 4 nightly CI runs, 2026-09-22 through 2026-09-25 (schedule event, RUN_FULL), on the self-hosted GitHub Actions runners ci-runner-2 and ci-runner-3: 1 vCPU / 6 GB RAM KVM guest on a shared N100 host, Ubuntu 24.04, .NET SDK 10.0.401. Both runners are provisioned identically and a run can land on either one; the four source runs are not attributed to a specific runner. Per-kernel spread across the four runs was 0 to 13.5 percent of the median (widest: cl-bench/median at 13.5%, tak at 10.4%). Runs from 2026-09-20 and earlier are excluded from the median: struct-slots and string-walk moved several-fold on 2026-09-22 when compiler fixes landed, so those older runs are a different regime, not noise; the 2026-09-19 nightly was cancelled and produced no numbers.
recorded.linux-x64@intel-core-i5-8350u-cpu-1-70gh: 2026-09-29, a Linux laptop used for A/B timing (Intel Core i5-8350U, 4 cores / 8 threads, 8 GB, Ubuntu 24.04, .NET SDK 10.0.112, powersave governor), median of 3 make bench-parity runs of 5 processes each. The three runs agreed to within 0.02 on every kernel. Recorded under its own key because the same commit gives ratios on this machine that differ from the CI runners by more than the threshold: on the commit the linux-x64 entries were measured on, this machine gave fib 4.51, fixnum-loop 1.91 and struct-slots 4.06 against the runners' 3.7, 1.0 and 2.87. cl-bench is not run by make bench-parity, so there is no cl-bench median here.

ratios.//fib: Lowered from 6.94 when (the fixnum ...) became a range license. The one contended parity run available measured 2.94; 4.00 is deliberately looser than that, because a ratio taken while another session was on the machine is not a number to gate on. Retake it with make bench-parity on a quiet machine and tighten.
